504	## Bindings — top-level `.flow` `bindings[]`
505	
506	When a flow uses connector nodes, the runtime needs to know **which authenticated connection** to use for each connector. Bindings are authored in the flow's **top-level `bindings[]` array** (a sibling of `nodes`, `edges`, `definitions`). At `flow debug` / `flow pack` time the CLI regenerates `content/bindings_v2.json` from these entries.
507	
508	> **Never edit `bindings_v2.json` directly.** Any manual edits are overwritten on the next debug/pack. All authoring flows through the `.flow` file's top-level `bindings[]`.
509	
510	### How connector nodes reference bindings
511	
512	The connector node's **definition** (the manifest copied from `uip maestro flow registry get` into `definitions[]`) carries a `model.context[]` template like this. **Leave the definition exactly as the registry returns it** — do NOT rewrite `<bindings.*>` placeholders inside the definition, and do NOT author `model.context[]` on the instance:
513	
514	```json
515	"context": [
516	  { "name": "connectorKey", "type": "string", "value": "uipath-atlassian-jira" },
517	  { "name": "connection", "type": "string", "value": "<bindings.uipath-atlassian-jira connection>" },
518	  { "name": "folderKey", "type": "string", "value": "<bindings.FolderKey>" }
519	]
520	```
521	
522	At BPMN emit time, the runtime rewrites each `<bindings.{name}>` placeholder to `=bindings.{id}` by finding a top-level `bindings[]` entry whose `name` matches the placeholder. For connectors the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` is typically unset, so matching is **name-only** within the `resource: "Connection"` candidate set.
523	
524	> **Matching differs from resource nodes.** For `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl), the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` is set to `<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>`, so placeholder matching is scoped by `(name, resourceKey)`. For connector nodes, `resourceKey` on the definition is typically unset, so matching is name-only — the `<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection` placeholder must be unique per connector in the flow. Don't confuse the two patterns.
525	
526	### Top-level `bindings[]` shape (CLI-emitted; reference only)
527	
528	`uip maestro flow node configure` populates these entries — you do not author them by hand. The schema below is the shape the CLI emits, for **inspection** when debugging a flow's binding state and as the planned shape for the **No-Live-Tenant** flow's sidecar `<nodeId>.detail.json` (see § No-Live-Tenant / Planned Configuration above). Per the [Author capability — Node ownership](../../../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node) rules, `bindings[]` is part of the CLI-owned envelope for connector / connector-trigger / managed HTTP nodes.
529	
530	For every unique connection used in the flow, `node configure` appends **two entries** to top-level `bindings[]`:
531	
532	```json
533	"bindings": [
534	  {
535	    "id": "<CONN_BINDING_ID>",
536	    "name": "<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection",
537	    "type": "string",
538	    "resource": "Connection",
539	    "resourceKey": "<CONNECTION_UUID>",
540	    "default": "<CONNECTION_UUID>",
541	    "propertyAttribute": "ConnectionId"
542	  },
543	  {
544	    "id": "<FOLDER_BINDING_ID>",
545	    "name": "FolderKey",
546	    "type": "string",
547	    "resource": "Connection",
548	    "resourceKey": "<CONNECTION_UUID>",
549	    "default": "<FOLDER_KEY>",
550	    "propertyAttribute": "FolderKey"
551	  }
552	]
553	```
554	
555	| Field | Value |
556	|-------|-------|
557	| `id` | Unique string within the file. Descriptive (e.g. `bJiraConn`) or short random (e.g. `bKEFLMRB2`). |
558	| `name` (connection binding) | The IS connection name (e.g. `"chandu.lella@uipath.com #3"`). `uip maestro flow node configure` fetches this from IS automatically — this is the supported path. The placeholder form `"<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection"` appears in the table for reference only (e.g. when inspecting a flow whose bindings have not yet been configured); it must match the definition's `model.context[].connection` placeholder (without the `<bindings.` prefix and `>` suffix). |
559	| `name` (folder binding) | Literal `"FolderKey"` — matches `<bindings.FolderKey>`. |
560	| `type` | Always `"string"`. |
561	| `resource` | Always `"Connection"` — capital C, case-sensitive. |
562	| `resourceKey` | The connection UUID from `uip is connections list`. **Same UUID on both bindings.** |
563	| `default` | Connection binding → connection UUID. Folder binding → folder key. |
564	| `propertyAttribute` | `"ConnectionId"` or `"FolderKey"` — case matters. |
565	
566	The connector node instance carries no `model` block and no binding/context data. `uip maestro flow node configure` populates only `inputs.detail` on the instance and appends the two top-level `bindings[]` entries. The connection UUID is held on the binding entry (`resourceKey`), not on the node.
567	
568	> **CLI side-effect — duplicate empty bindings.** `node configure` currently appends placeholder entries with `resourceKey: ""` and no `default` alongside the resolved pair (4 entries per configure call instead of 2). Validate passes; they're harmless but verbose. Remove the empty pair via `Edit` after configure if you care about clean diffs.
569	
570	**Share bindings across nodes using the same connection.** If two connector nodes share the same `<CONNECTION_UUID>`, reuse the same two binding entries — do not add duplicates. Matching is by `name` only (the `<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection` placeholder is unique per connector), so any node whose definition resolves against `<bindings.<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection>` picks up the shared binding pair.
571	
572	### Single-connector example (Jira)
573	
574	```json
575	"bindings": [
576	  {
577	    "id": "bJiraConn",
578	    "name": "uipath-atlassian-jira connection",
579	    "type": "string",
580	    "resource": "Connection",
581	    "resourceKey": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
582	    "default": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
583	    "propertyAttribute": "ConnectionId"
584	  },
585	  {
586	    "id": "bJiraFolder",
587	    "name": "FolderKey",
588	    "type": "string",
589	    "resource": "Connection",
590	    "resourceKey": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
591	    "default": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",

610	Both `FolderKey` entries share the same `name` but have distinct `resourceKey`s — that's how the runtime keeps them separate.
611	
612	### Generated `bindings_v2.json` (reference only — do not edit)
613	
614	At debug/pack time, the CLI derives `content/bindings_v2.json` from the top-level `bindings[]` above. One `Connection` resource per unique `resourceKey`; the `FolderKey` bindings are absorbed as metadata (they do not produce standalone resource entries). The generated output looks like:
615	
616	```json
617	{
618	  "version": "2.0",
619	  "resources": [
620	    {
621	      "resource": "Connection",
622	      "key": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
623	      "id": "Connection7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
624	      "value": {
625	        "ConnectionId": {
626	          "defaultValue": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
627	          "isExpression": false,
628	          "displayName": "my-jira-connection"
629	        }
630	      },

632	        "ActivityName": "Create Issue",

643	- `id` is always `"Connection" + <resourceKey>` (concatenated, no separator) — generated, not authored.
644	- `metadata.Connector` is derived from the definition's `model.context[].connectorKey`.
645	- `metadata.ActivityName` comes from the matched node's `display.label`.

648	
649	For connector-trigger flows, the same pattern applies — top-level `bindings[]` entries with additional metadata; the CLI derives `EventTrigger` and `Property` resources for `bindings_v2.json`. See [connector-trigger/impl.md](../connector-trigger/impl.md) for the trigger-specific shape.

662	## Debug
663	
664	### Common Errors
665	
666	| Error | Cause | Fix |
667	| --- | --- | --- |
668	| No connection found | Connection not bound — top-level `bindings[]` missing or `resourceKey` doesn't match the node | Run Step 1 above to bind a connection; verify both entries (`ConnectionId` + `FolderKey`) are in the top-level `bindings[]` |
669	| Connection ping failed | Connection expired or misconfigured | Re-authenticate the connection in the IS portal |
670	| Missing `inputs.detail` | Node added but not configured | Run `uip maestro flow node configure` with the detail JSON (Step 6) |
671	| Reference field has display name instead of ID | `uip is resources run list` was skipped | Resolve the reference field to get the actual ID (Step 4) |
672	| Node faults at runtime with "resource not found" or similar after a clean build and validate | Reference field uses an ID scoped to a **different** connection (common when copying from a prior flow in the same session — e.g., a Slack channel ID from workspace A pasted into a node bound to workspace B's connection) | Re-run `uip is resources run list "<connector-key>" "<objectName>" --connection-id <CURRENT_CONNECTION_ID>`, extract the fresh ID, update `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters` in `--detail`, re-run `node configure`, re-debug. See Step 4 and the top-level Anti-Pattern on reference-ID reuse in [SKILL.md](../../../../../SKILL.md). |
673	| Required field missing at runtime | Required input field not provided | Check metadataFile for all `required: true` fields in both `requestFields` and `parameters` |
674	| `$vars` expression unresolvable | Node outputs block missing or node not connected | Verify the node has edges and upstream outputs are correctly referenced |
675	| `connectorMethodInfo` missing method/path | Used `registry get` without `--connection-id` | Re-run with `--connection-id` for enriched metadata (Step 2) |
676	| `bindings_v2.json` malformed or stale | It was hand-edited (the CLI overwrites edits on next debug/pack), or top-level `bindings[]` was mutated by hand | Never edit `bindings_v2.json` directly. Re-run `uip maestro flow node configure` on the affected connector node(s) so the CLI re-emits top-level `bindings[]`; `bindings_v2.json` is regenerated from those at the next debug/pack. Compare the emitted shape against the CLI-emitted reference in § Top-level `bindings[]` shape. |
677	| Connector key not found | Wrong key name | Run `uip is connectors list --output json` — keys are often prefixed with `uipath-` |

1	# UiPath Flow File Format
2	
3	The `.flow` file is a JSON document at `<ProjectName>.flow` in the project root. It is the **only file you should edit** — other generated files will be overwritten.
4	
5	## Table of contents
6	
7	- [Top-level structure](#top-level-structure)
8	- [Project structure (from `uip maestro flow init`)](#project-structure-from-uip-maestro-flow-init)
9	- [Node instance](#node-instance)
10	- [Layout](#layout)
11	- [Edge — both ports required](#edge--both-ports-required)
12	- [Definition entry](#definition-entry)
13	- [Common node types](#common-node-types)
14	- [Standard ports by node type](#standard-ports-by-node-type)
15	- [Implicit error port on action nodes](#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes)
16	- [Minimal working example — dice roller](#minimal-working-example--dice-roller)
17	- [entry-points.json — auto-generated, do not edit](#entry-pointsjson--auto-generated-do-not-edit)
18	- [Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings (top-level `bindings[]`)](#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings)
19	- [Bindings — connector connection binding](#bindings--connector-connection-binding)
20	
21	## Top-level structure
22	
23	```json
24	{
25	  "id": "<uuid>",
26	  "version": "<version from `uip maestro flow init`>",
27	  "name": "MyFlow",
28	  "nodes": [],
29	  "edges": [],
30	  "definitions": [],
31	  "bindings": [],
32	  "variables": {},
33	  "layout": {
34	    "nodes": {}
35	  }
36	}
37	```
38	
39	> **Key order is NOT guaranteed — never anchor edits on it.** The skeleton above is illustrative; the CLI does not commit to a stable top-level key sequence or to which optional keys are present. Real flows vary: `runtime` may appear (and has been observed *before* `nodes`, not after `definitions`) or be absent entirely; `bindings`, `variables`, `solutionId`, `projectId`, and a trailing `metadata` object surface in different positions depending on CLI version and what the flow contains. When editing a `.flow`, anchor each `Edit` on the **target array's own key** (`"nodes": [`, `"edges": [`, `"definitions": [`, or `layout.nodes`) located in the text you just `Read` — never on "the key that follows X." See [greenfield.md — Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits](../author/references/greenfield.md#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order).
40	
41	Optional top-level `runtime`: a CLI-managed object that appears on some flows (e.g. after `uip maestro flow node add` for an HTTP/connector node) and is absent on others. It is not user-authored — do not add, remove, or anchor on it. Its presence and position are not guaranteed.
42	
43	**Top-level `version`** = workflow file-format version. **Use the exact value `uip maestro flow init` scaffolds** — do not hand-pick, hardcode, or downgrade it. It is not a semver string; the schema gates on an exact literal for the current file-format version, so an older value (e.g. `"1.0"`, `"1.0.0"`) that worked for a legacy parser will fail for a new flow. `init` always writes the accepted value; preserve it. To see the current value, scaffold a throwaway flow with `init` and read its top-level `version`, or read it from an existing `init`-generated `.flow`.
44	
45	> **Don't confuse top-level `version` with `definitions[].version` / `typeVersion`.** Node-definition `version` (and matching node-instance `typeVersion`) are validated by `versionSchema`, a regex that accepts both `x.y` and `x.y.z` (`/^\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?$/`, error `'Version must be in format "x.y" or "x.y.z"'`). Both layers are canonically `x.y`, but the node-level regex still accepts legacy 3-part strings so registry definitions (`"1.0"`) and older scaffolded nodes (`"1.0.0"`) both parse. The two layers report distinct errors, but Zod may collapse a node-level mismatch to path `(root)`. If you see a version-related error at `(root)`, audit the top-level `version` first; if it's correct, check each node's `typeVersion` against the matching `definitions[].version`.
46	
47	`solutionId` and `projectId` may also appear at the top level — these are auto-populated by `uip maestro flow init` and packaging. Do not add them manually.
48	
49	> **`bindings[]`** holds Orchestrator resource references for `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl) and for connector-node connections. See [Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings](#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings) below and the [connector plugin](../author/references/plugins/connector/impl.md) for the connector-binding shape.
50	
51	## Project structure (from `uip maestro flow init`)
52	
53	```
54	<ProjectName>/
55	├── project.uiproj          # { "Name": "...", "ProjectType": "Flow" }
56	├── <ProjectName>.flow      # ← edit this
57	├── bindings_v2.json        # resource bindings
58	├── entry-points.json       # input/output schema declarations
59	├── operate.json            # runtime options
60	└── package-descriptor.json # packaging manifest
61	```
62	
63	## Node instance
64	
65	```json
66	{
67	  "id": "rollDice",
68	  "type": "core.action.script",
69	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
70	  "display": { "label": "Roll Dice" },
71	  "inputs": {
72	    "script": "return { roll: Math.floor(Math.random() * 6) + 1 };"
73	  },
74	  "outputs": {
75	    "output": {
76	      "type": "object",
77	      "description": "The return value of the script",
78	      "source": "=result.response",
79	      "var": "output"
80	    },
81	    "error": {
82	      "type": "object",
83	      "description": "Error information if the script fails",
84	      "source": "=result.Error",
85	      "var": "error"
86	    }
87	  }
88	}
89	```
90	
91	**Required fields on every node**: `id`, `type`, `typeVersion`, **`display`** (with at least a `label`). This applies to **every** node — triggers (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers), action nodes, control-flow nodes (`core.control.end`, `core.logic.terminate`), and human-task nodes. The Zod `nodeSchema` declares `display: displayConfigSchema` without `.optional()`, so no node type is exempt — even ones that "feel" trivial.
92	
93	`typeVersion` must match the corresponding `definitions[].version` exactly. The registry often returns versions such as `"1.0"` while older examples or scaffolded files may show `"1.0.0"`. If a node uses `typeVersion: "1.0.0"` but the copied definition is `"version": "1.0"`, validation reports "Node type `<type>:1.0.0` has no matching definition." When direct-authoring a new node from `registry get`, set `typeVersion` to the copied definition's `version`; when preserving an existing node, preserve its existing node/definition pair unless you intentionally update both together. <!-- version-check-skip --> (explains the x.y vs x.y.z mismatch mechanic; literals are illustrative, not pinned)
94	
95	> **Gotcha — vague schema-validation error on missing `display`.** Omitting `display` on any node produces:
96	>
97	> ```
98	> [error] [(root)] Schema validation failed: Invalid input: expected object, received undefined
99	> ```
100	>
101	> The error path is `(root)` and does NOT pinpoint which node or which field is missing. If you see this error after editing a `.flow` file, audit every node for a `display` block before doing anything else.
102	
103	> **No instance `model` block.** BPMN type, serviceType, event definition, and binding/context templates all live in the node's **definition** (the manifest copied from the registry into `definitions[]`). The runtime hydrates them from the definition at serialization time — instances carry only per-instance data (`inputs`, `outputs`, `display`). This applies to every inline-agent-related node too: `uipath.agent.autonomous` plus every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) carries source identity at `inputs.source`. Their definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists that identity onto each instance's `inputs.source`. Do not write a `"model": { "source": ... }` block on the instance.
104	>
105	> **No `ui` block on nodes.** Position and size are stored in the top-level `layout` object, not on individual nodes. See [Layout](#layout) below.
106	
107	### Instance-specific identity fields
108	
109	A few per-instance identity fields live on the node instance:
110	
111	| Field | Used by | Purpose |
112	|-------|---------|---------|
113	| `inputs.entryPointId` | All trigger nodes (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers) | Stable UUID identifying the entry point |
114	| `inputs.isDefaultEntryPoint` | Trigger nodes in subflows | Boolean marking the default entry point when a subflow has multiple triggers |
115	| `inputs.source` | `uipath.agent.autonomous` and every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) | For `uipath.agent.autonomous`: the inline agent's `projectId`. For resource nodes: the attached resource UUID. Definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists onto the instance — no instance `model` block. |
116	| `inputs.color`, `inputs.content` | Sticky-note nodes | Visual content of the sticky note |
117	
118	Example — manual start trigger:
119	
120	```json
121	{
122	  "id": "start",
123	  "type": "core.trigger.manual",
124	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
125	  "display": { "label": "Manual trigger" },
126	  "inputs": {
127	    "entryPointId": "3d4a8c34-5682-4ebe-a6bc-d92a18830bb5"
128	  },
129	  "outputs": {
130	    "output": { "type": "object", "description": "The return value of the trigger.", "source": "=result.response", "var": "output" }
131	  }
132	}
133	```
134	
135	### Node outputs
136	
137	`$vars.<sourceNodeId>.<outputId>` resolution at runtime is driven by **`variables.nodes[]`**, not by the node instance's `outputs` block. The BPMN emitter walks `variables.nodes[]` to write the process-level `<uipath:inputOutput id="<nodeId>.<outputId>">` declarations the runtime needs; the action-node instance `outputs` block is ignored at serialization (the manifest's `outputDefinition` supplies the activity-side mapping). End / terminate nodes are the exception — their instance `outputs` block IS consumed to map workflow-level `out` variables. See [end/impl.md](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md).
138	
139	The canonical recipe for a data-producing node is therefore:
140	
141	- `definitions[]` entry copied verbatim from `uip maestro flow registry get` (carries the manifest `outputDefinition`).
142	- `variables.nodes[]` entry per output: `{ "id": "<nodeId>.<outputId>", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "<nodeId>", "outputId": "<outputId>" } }`.
143	- Optional instance `outputs` block matching the manifest — harmless and matches the canonical examples below for clarity, but **not** what controls runtime variable visibility.
144	
145	Skipping `variables.nodes[]` produces a flow that passes `flow validate` but resolves `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` to `undefined` at runtime (MST-9972). `uip maestro flow format` regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from `nodes[]` + `definitions[]`, so always run it after structural edits — the omission becomes self-healing.
146	
147	When you DO author the instance `outputs` block (for documentation / parity with manifest schema), use the shape below. Each output entry has:
148	
149	- `type` — data type (usually `"object"`)
150	- `description` — human-readable description
151	- `source` — runtime binding expression (e.g., `"=result.response"` for the primary output, `"=result.Error"` for errors)
152	- `var` — the variable name (matches the output ID, e.g., `"output"`, `"error"`)
153	
154	The standard `outputs` block for most action nodes (script, HTTP, transform, connector, agent):
155	
156	```json
157	"outputs": {
158	  "output": {
159	    "type": "object",
160	    "description": "The return value of the <node type>",
161	    "source": "=result.response",
162	    "var": "output"
163	  },
164	  "error": {
165	    "type": "object",
166	    "description": "Error information if the <node type> fails",
167	    "source": "=result.Error",
168	    "var": "error"
169	  }
170	}
171	```
172	
173	Trigger nodes (manual, scheduled, connector triggers) have a single output — no error port:
174	
175	```json
176	"outputs": {
177	  "output": {
178	    "type": "object",
179	    "description": "The return value of the trigger.",
180	    "source": "=result.response",
181	    "var": "output"
182	  }
183	}
184	```
185	
186	End/terminate nodes do **not** use this pattern — their `outputs` maps workflow-level output variables (see the [Author end plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md)).
187	
188	## Layout
189	
190	Node positioning is stored in a **top-level `layout` object**, keyed by node `id`. The same shape applies inside each subflow as `subflows[<id>].layout`. Layout data is owned by `uip maestro flow format` (see [cli-commands.md](cli-commands.md#uip-maestro-flow-format)) — you should not need to hand-write it.
191	
192	```json
193	"layout": {
194	  "nodes": {
195	    "start": {
196	      "position": { "x": 200, "y": 144 },
197	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
198	      "collapsed": false
199	    },
200	    "rollDice": {
201	      "position": { "x": 400, "y": 144 },
202	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
203	      "collapsed": false
204	    },
205	    "end": {
206	      "position": { "x": 600, "y": 144 },
207	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
208	      "collapsed": false
209	    }
210	  }
211	}
212	```
213	
214	Each key in `layout.nodes` is a node `id`. `flow format` creates an entry for every node and populates `position` + `size`.
215	
216	**What format does:**
217	- Arranges nodes horizontally (left-to-right) with `nodeSpacing: 96`, anchored to the leftmost node's original position
218	- Sets each node's `size` to match its canvas shape: inline agents (`uipath.agent.autonomous` / `uipath.agent.conversational`, `shape: rectangle`) → `{ "width": 288, "height": 96 }`; containers (loops/groups) → `{ "width": 560, "height": 320 }`; everything else — including referenced `uipath.core.agent.<guid>` nodes — → `{ "width": 96, "height": 96 }`. A size that disagrees with the node's shape renders misshapen in Studio Web.
219	- Skips `stickyNote` nodes from layout (they keep their custom position and size)
220	- Recurses into every subflow and rewrites its `subflows[<id>].layout` map
221	
222	**Subflow layout is scoped.** Each subflow entry in `subflows[<id>]` has its **own** `layout.nodes` map for the nodes inside that subflow — they do NOT live in the top-level `layout.nodes`. Format handles both passes. See the [Author subflow plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/subflow/impl.md).
223	
224	## Edge — both ports required
225	
226	```json
227	{
228	  "id": "edge-start-rollDice",
229	  "sourceNodeId": "start",
230	  "sourcePort": "output",
231	  "targetNodeId": "rollDice",
232	  "targetPort": "input"
233	}
234	```
235	
236	> **Gotcha**: `targetPort` is required. Omitting it produces `[error] [edges[N].targetPort] Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` at validate time.
237	>
238	> **Gotcha**: the source field is `sourcePort`, not `sourceHandle`. If you write `sourceHandle`, validation fails with `[error] [edges[N].sourcePort] Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` — the path identifies the offending edge entry exactly.
239	
240	## Definition entry
241	
242	Every node type appearing in `nodes` must have a matching entry in `definitions`. Get the correct definition from:
243	
244	```bash
245	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.script --output json
246	```
247	
248	Copy the returned node definition object into your `definitions` array. Depending on CLI/plugin version, that object may appear at `Data.Node` or as the top-level object containing fields such as `nodeType`, `version`, and `handleConfiguration`. Do not write definitions by hand — always pull from the registry to ensure schema compliance.
249	
250	## Common node types
251	
252	| Type | Purpose | Key inputs |
253	|------|---------|------------|
254	| `core.trigger.manual` | Entry point | `entryPointId` |
255	| `core.trigger.scheduled` | Recurring schedule trigger | `entryPointId`, `timerType`, `timerPreset` |
256	| `core.action.script` | Run JavaScript | `script` |
257	| `core.action.http.v2` | HTTP request | `method`, `url`, `headers`, `body` |
258	| `core.action.transform` | Map/filter/group data | `collection`, `operations` |
259	| `core.logic.decision` | If/else branch | `expression` |
260	| `core.logic.switch` | Multi-way branch | `cases` |
261	| `core.logic.loop` | Iterate collection | `collection`, `parallel` |
262	| `core.logic.merge` | Sync parallel paths | — |
263	| `core.control.end` | Graceful end | — |
264	| `core.logic.terminate` | Abort workflow | — |
265	
266	> The BPMN type for each node (e.g., `bpmn:StartEvent`, `bpmn:ScriptTask`) lives in the `definitions` entry copied from `uip maestro flow registry get`. Instances do not carry the BPMN type.
267	
268	For full details on each node (ports, inputs, outputs, when to use), see the [Author planning architecture guide](../author/references/planning-arch.md). For implementation resolution (registry lookups, connection binding, reference field resolution), see the [Author planning implementation guide](../author/references/planning-impl.md).
269	
270	Discover all available types:
271	```bash
272	uip maestro flow registry list --output json
273	uip maestro flow registry search <keyword>
274	```

276	## Standard ports by node type
277	
278	| Node type | Source ports (outgoing) | Target ports (incoming) |
279	|-----------|------------------------|------------------------|

300	## Implicit error port on action nodes
301	
302	Any node with `supportsErrorHandling: true` in the registry exposes an implicit `error` source port for catching node-level failures. This applies to HTTP, Script, Transform (all variants), connector activities, agent nodes, and RPA nodes — essentially every action node.
303	
304	The port is **not** listed in the registry's `handleConfiguration`. Studio Web only exposes it when the source node has `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true`; when the flow contains an outgoing edge with `sourcePort: "error"` from that node, the serializer emits a BPMN boundary error event attached to the node. Because of this gate, `uip maestro flow validate` reports an error when a node has an outgoing `sourcePort: "error"` edge but `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled` is not `true` — so the inconsistency is caught before publish rather than surfacing as a hidden edge in Studio Web.
305	
306	### When the error port fires
307	
308	- Network failures, DNS errors, TLS errors
309	- Request timeouts
310	- Non-2xx HTTP responses (unless caught by a configured `inputs.branches` entry)
311	- Script exceptions (`throw`, undefined reference, etc.)
312	- Transform operation failures (invalid collection, missing field)
313	- Any unhandled runtime exception inside the node
314	
315	Without a wired error edge, any of these fails the whole flow with `finalStatus: "Faulted"`.
316	
317	### Wiring the error port
318	
319	```bash
320	# Confirm the node supports error handling
321	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json --output-filter "Node.SupportsErrorHandling"
322	
323	# Add an outgoing edge with sourcePort: "error"
324	uip maestro flow edge add <Project>.flow <actionNodeId> <errorHandlerId> \
325	  --source-port error --target-port input --output json
326	```
327	
328	`uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true` on the source node automatically. When editing `.flow` JSON directly, set the flag yourself:
329	
330	```json
331	{
332	  "id": "<actionNodeId>",
333	  "inputs": {
334	    "errorHandlingEnabled": true
335	  }
336	}
337	```
338	
339	Inside the error handler, `$vars.{actionNodeId}.error` resolves to the error object. For HTTP it's `{ code, message, detail, category, status }`; other nodes have similar shapes — check the node's `outputDefinition.error.schema` in the registry.
340	
341	### Error port vs other branching
342	
343	| Mechanism | When to use |
344	| --- | --- |
345	| **`error` source port** (any action node) | The node failed (exception, timeout, non-2xx not caught by a branch). Generic "something went wrong" handler. |
346	| **`branch-{id}` ports** (HTTP only, `inputs.branches`) | The call succeeded and you want to route on response *content* — different paths for e.g. empty vs non-empty results. |
347	| **`core.logic.decision` downstream** | Simple yes/no routing on the node's successful output. Doesn't help if the node itself fails. |
348	| **`core.logic.switch` downstream** | Multi-way routing on the node's successful output. Same — doesn't catch failures. |

467	## entry-points.json — auto-generated, do not edit
468	
469	`entry-points.json` declares the flow's external interface (input/output schemas and trigger entry points). **Do not edit this file directly** — it is auto-generated by `uip maestro flow init` and regenerated by `uip maestro flow debug` before upload. Manual edits will be overwritten.

478	## Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings (top-level `bindings[]`)
479	
480	The top-level `bindings` array (a sibling of `nodes`, `edges`, `definitions`, `variables`, `layout`) holds resource-reference indirections for **Orchestrator resource nodes** — RPA workflows, agents, flows, agentic processes, API workflows, and HITL apps.
481	
482	Each resource node needs two binding entries (one for `name`, one for `folderPath`). The node instance itself has no binding or context data — just `inputs`. The definition (copied verbatim from the registry) carries `model.context[]` templates like `<bindings.name>` and `<bindings.folderPath>`. At BPMN emit time the runtime rewrites those placeholders to `=bindings.<id>` by matching the placeholder name against a workflow-level binding, scoped by the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey`.
483	
484	```json
485	"bindings": [
486	  {
487	    "id": "<UNIQUE_ID>",
488	    "name": "name",
489	    "type": "string",
490	    "resource": "process",
491	    "resourceKey": "<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>",
492	    "default": "<ResourceName>",
493	    "propertyAttribute": "name",
494	    "resourceSubType": "Process"
495	  },
496	  {
497	    "id": "<UNIQUE_ID_2>",
498	    "name": "folderPath",
499	    "type": "string",
500	    "resource": "process",
501	    "resourceKey": "<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>",
502	    "default": "<FolderPath>",
503	    "propertyAttribute": "folderPath",
504	    "resourceSubType": "Process"
505	  }
506	]
507	```
508	
509	**Rules:**
510	
511	- Add **two entries** per resource node (one for `name`, one for `folderPath`).
512	- **Share** entries across node instances that reference the same resource — do not duplicate. Matching is by `(resourceKey, name)`, so any node whose definition has the same `resourceKey` resolves to the same binding pair.
513	- Entry IDs are unique strings within the file. Descriptive IDs (e.g. `bDepositRpaName`) are preferred over short random IDs.
514	- The node instance has no `model` block — it carries only `inputs`, `outputs`, and `display`.
515	- `resourceKey` must exactly match the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` (verbatim from the registry). The runtime uses this key to scope placeholder resolution so that binding names like `name` / `folderPath` (shared across resource kinds) don't cross-alias.
516	- `resourceSubType` mirrors the definition's `model.bindings.resourceSubType`: `Process` (rpa), `Agent` (agent), `Flow` (flow), `ProcessOrchestration` (agentic-process), `Api` (api-workflow), or the app type for HITL.
517	
518	**Why this is required.** The definition's `model.context[].value` fields are placeholders of the form `<bindings.{name}>` — deliberately invalid as runtime expressions, so they can't be confused with one. Before the BPMN is emitted, the runtime rewrites each placeholder to `=bindings.<id>` by finding a workflow-level binding with `(resourceKey, name)` matching the node's manifest `model.bindings.resourceKey` + the placeholder name. Without matching entries in top-level `bindings[]`, `uip maestro flow debug` fails with "Folder does not exist or the user does not have access to the folder" even though `uip maestro flow validate` passes.
519	
520	**Definitions stay verbatim.** Do NOT rewrite `<bindings.*>` placeholders inside the `definitions` entry — the definition is the authoring template. See "Every node type needs a `definitions` entry" in [author/CAPABILITY.md](../author/CAPABILITY.md).
521	
522	See each resource plugin's `impl.md` for the full JSON per node type: [rpa](../author/references/plugins/rpa/impl.md), [agent](../author/references/plugins/agent/impl.md), [flow](../author/references/plugins/flow/impl.md), [agentic-process](../author/references/plugins/agentic-process/impl.md), [api-workflow](../author/references/plugins/api-workflow/impl.md), [hitl](../author/references/plugins/hitl/impl.md).
523	
524	**Not to be confused with `bindings_v2.json`.** That file holds connector connection bindings for Integration Service nodes — a separate system. A flow may have both: a top-level `bindings[]` for resource references and a `bindings_v2.json` file for connector connections.

65	## Filter Trees (CEQL)
66	
67	Some IS activities — most notably **List All Records** and other list/query operations — accept a server-side filter expressed in **CEQL** (Connector Expression Query Language). As with trigger filters (which compile to JMESPath), CEQL filters are authored as a **structured filter tree** and the CLI compiles them to a CEQL string. Authoring as a tree keeps the CLI and Studio Web in lockstep so the activity round-trips cleanly when re-opened in SW.
68	
69	### Contract — three signals from IS metadata
70	
71	The CLI reads the live IS metadata response and uses three signals to wire the filter:
72	
73	1. **The activity supports CEQL** when one of its `parameters` declares `design.component === "FilterBuilder"`. That parameter's `name` is the connector-specific key the compiled CEQL string is sent under — most commonly `where`, but **not always** (e.g. Salesforce uses `q`). Activities with no such parameter do not support server-side filtering — pass no `filter` and filter downstream.
74	2. **A field is filterable** when its IS metadata entry has `searchable: true`. Type alone does not gate it — the connector flags fields explicitly. Fields without `searchable: true` are rejected by the CLI even if they look like primitives.
75	3. **Permitted operators** for the field are listed under `searchableOperators`. **Connector-side identifier** for the field in CEQL is `searchableNames[0]` when present (some connectors expose a friendly `name` but require a different identifier in the query string).
76	
77	### What the CLI persists from a single `filter` input
78	
79	- **Runtime side** — the compiled CEQL string lands at `inputs.detail.queryParameters.<filterParamName>` where `<filterParamName>` is the FilterBuilder parameter's name from the IS metadata (often `where`).
80	- **Design-time side** — the structured tree is embedded under `inputs.detail.configuration`'s `essentialConfiguration.savedFilterTrees.<filterParamName>`. Studio Web reads this on open to re-render the filter widget; without it the filter UI shows up empty even though the runtime call still works.
81	
82	Pass `filter` (the structured tree) and the CLI emits both halves in lockstep. Passing both `filter` and `queryParameters.<filterParamName>` is rejected at validation time — single source of truth.
83	
84	### Tree shape
85	
86	Identical to the trigger filter tree — the same `FilterTree` / `Filter` / `WorkflowValue` types are used; only the compiler output (CEQL vs JMESPath) differs.
87	
88	```jsonc
89	{
90	  "groupOperator": 0,             // 0 = And, 1 = Or — combines sibling filters/groups
91	  "index": 0,                     // ordering index within parent (root is 0)
92	  "filters": [                    // leaf conditions at this level
93	    {
94	      "id": "<fieldName>",        // resource field name from `is resources describe`
95	      "operator": "<Operator>",   // PascalCase, see operator table below
96	      "value": {
97	        "value": <typed value>,   // string / number / boolean / ISO-8601 date-time / array
98	        "rawString": "\"...\"",   // verbatim user-entered text (with quotes for strings)
99	        "isLiteral": true         // literals only — expression values are not yet supported
100	      }
101	    }
102	  ],
103	  "groups": []                    // optional: nested subgroups (same shape as root)
104	}
105	```
106	
107	A no-op filter — used when the user wants to list all records without restriction — is `null` or `{"groupOperator": null, "index": 0, "filters": []}`. Prefer **omitting** the `filter` field entirely.
108	
109	### Compiled CEQL output
110	
111	The CLI compiles each leaf to `<field> <op> <value>` (or `<field> <function>` for null checks) and joins siblings with the group operator. String values are wrapped in single quotes; booleans, numerics, and enums are passed bare.
112	
113	| Operator | CEQL token | Notes |
114	|---|---|---|
115	| `Equals` | `=` | |
116	| `NotEquals` | `!=` | |
117	| `LessThan` / `LessThanOrEqual` / `GreaterThan` / `GreaterThanOrEqual` | `<` / `<=` / `>` / `>=` | Numeric / date-time |
118	| `Contains` / `NotContains` | `Contains` / `Not Contains` | Substring (string) |
119	| `StartsWith` / `NotStartsWith` / `EndsWith` / `NotEndsWith` | `Starts With` / `Not Starts With` / `Ends With` / `Not Ends With` | String |
120	| `Like` / `NotLike` | `Like` / `Not Like` | Pattern match (connector-specific) |
121	| `In` / `NotIn` | `In` / `Not In` | Membership — `value.value` is a list; rendered as `(v1, v2, …)` |
122	| `IsNull` / `IsNotNull` | `Is Null` / `Is Not Null` | No `value` needed |
123	| `Is` / `IsNot` | `=` against literal `true` / `false` | Boolean shortcut |
124	
125	Logical operators between siblings:
126	
127	| `groupOperator` | CEQL token |
128	|---|---|
129	| `0` (And) | ` AND ` |
130	| `1` (Or) | ` OR ` |
131	
132	### Examples
133	
134	**Active accounts only:**
135	
136	```json
137	{
138	  "groupOperator": 0, "index": 0,
139	  "filters": [
140	    { "id": "Status", "operator": "Equals",
141	      "value": { "value": "Active", "rawString": "\"Active\"", "isLiteral": true } }
142	  ]
143	}
144	```
145	→ CEQL: `Status = 'Active'`
146	
147	**Score ≥ 80 AND Region in (EMEA, APAC):**
148	
149	```json
150	{
151	  "groupOperator": 0, "index": 0,
152	  "filters": [
153	    { "id": "Score", "operator": "GreaterThanOrEqual",
154	      "value": { "value": 80, "rawString": "80", "isLiteral": true } },
155	    { "id": "Region", "operator": "In",
156	      "value": { "value": ["EMEA", "APAC"], "rawString": "[\"EMEA\",\"APAC\"]", "isLiteral": true } }
157	  ]
158	}
159	```
160	→ CEQL: `Score >= 80 AND Region In ('EMEA', 'APAC')`
161	
162	**Subject contains "urgent" AND (owner = me OR owner is null):**
163	
164	```json
165	{
166	  "groupOperator": 0, "index": 0,
167	  "filters": [
168	    { "id": "Subject", "operator": "Contains",
169	      "value": { "value": "urgent", "rawString": "\"urgent\"", "isLiteral": true } }
170	  ],
171	  "groups": [
172	    {
173	      "groupOperator": 1, "index": 1,
174	      "filters": [
175	        { "id": "OwnerId", "operator": "Equals",
176	          "value": { "value": "${me.id}", "rawString": "\"${me.id}\"", "isLiteral": false } },
177	        { "id": "OwnerId", "operator": "IsNull" }
178	      ]
179	    }
180	  ]
181	}
182	```
183	→ CEQL: `Subject Contains 'urgent' AND (OwnerId = ${me.id} OR OwnerId Is Null)`. Non-literal values (`isLiteral: false`) are emitted as `${expression}` placeholders for runtime resolution.
184	
185	### How to build a CEQL filter tree
186	
187	1. Run `uip is resources describe "<connector-key>" "<objectName>" --connection-id "<id>" --operation List` to read the resource's metadata.
188	2. **Confirm CEQL is supported** for this operation: at least one entry under `parameters` must carry `design.component === "FilterBuilder"`. If none does, the activity does not support server-side filtering — omit `filter` and filter downstream (e.g. with a Script node).
189	3. **Pick filterable fields** from `fields[]` where `searchable: true`. Other fields will be rejected by the CLI at configure time even if they look like primitives.
190	4. For each leaf, pick an operator from the field's `searchableOperators` list (when present). Date-time fields take ISO-8601 strings; enums take the literal enum value.
191	5. Use the field's `name` as the leaf `id`. The CLI rewrites it to `searchableNames[0]` when emitting CEQL if the connector declares one — you don't need to use the alias yourself.
192	6. Build one leaf per condition; place multiple conditions under the same `groupOperator` (0 for AND, 1 for OR). Use nested `groups` for mixed AND/OR.
193	7. Wrap values in a `WorkflowValue` object with `value`, `rawString`, `isLiteral`. Strings, numbers, booleans, dates, and arrays are all valid `value` types; only `isLiteral: true` is currently supported by activity-side compilation.
194	
195	### What NOT to generate
196	
197	| Invalid input | Why it fails | Valid replacement |
198	|---|---|---|
199	| `"filter": "Status = 'Active'"` | Bare CEQL string — `filter` must be an object. | Structured tree with `filters: [...]`. |
200	| `"filterExpression": "..."` | That field is reserved for the trigger (JMESPath) path. | Use `filter` (CEQL tree) for activities. |
201	| `{ "operator": "equals", ... }` | Operator is case-sensitive. | `"operator": "Equals"` |
202	| `{ "value": "Active" }` on a leaf | Bare string — must be wrapped in the `WorkflowValue` object. | `{ "value": { "value": "Active", "rawString": "\"Active\"", "isLiteral": true } }` |
203	| `{ "id": "fields.Status", ... }` | `fields.` prefix — use the bare field name from `is resources describe`. | `{ "id": "Status", ... }` |

1	# Action Node Structure
2	
3	Reference for the boilerplate shared by every action-node `impl.md` in this skill. Plugin docs should link here for the standard parts and only spell out what is plugin-specific: the registry type string, plugin-specific input fields, plugin-specific rules, debug entries, and node-type configuration workflows.
4	
5	## Registry validation
6	
7	Every action node should validate its registry contract before authoring:
8	
9	```bash
10	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json
11	```
12	
13	`registry get` returns the manifest at `Data.Node`. Do **not** inspect `Data` directly as if it were the node manifest.
14	
15	```json
16	{
17	  "Data": {
18	    "Node": {
19	      "nodeType": "core.action.script",
20	      "version": "1.0",
21	      "handleConfiguration": [
22	        { "position": "left", "handles": [{ "id": "input", "type": "target" }] },
23	        { "position": "right", "handles": [{ "id": "success", "type": "source" }] }
24	      ],
25	      "inputDefinition": {},
26	      "outputDefinition": {}
27	    }
28	  }
29	}
30	```
31	
32	Inspect:
33	
34	- `Data.Node.handleConfiguration` — input port name and output port name(s). Array of position groups, not a map with a top-level `handles` field.
35	- `Data.Node.inputDefinition` — required inputs.
36	- `Data.Node.outputDefinition` — downstream payloads.
37	- `Data.Node.model.serviceType` — where applicable.
38	
39	Plugin `impl.md` records what to confirm for that specific node type.
40	
41	## Standard JSON skeleton
42	
43	All action nodes share this base shape on the node instance:
44	
45	```json
46	{
47	  "id": "<nodeId>",
48	  "type": "<node-type>",
49	  "typeVersion": "<version>",
50	  "display": { "label": "<Label>" },
51	  "inputs": { /* plugin-specific — see plugin impl.md */ },
52	  "outputs": {
53	    "output": {
54	      "type": "object",
55	      "description": "<plugin-specific description>",
56	      "source": "=result.response",
57	      "var": "output"
58	    },
59	    "error": {
60	      "type": "object",
61	      "description": "Error information if the action fails.",
62	      "source": "=result.Error",
63	      "var": "error"
64	    }
65	  }
66	}
67	```
68	
69	`outputs.output` documents the success payload referenced downstream as `=js:$vars.{nodeId}.output`. `outputs.error` documents the failure shape; the runtime routes to the implicit `error` port when the action faults. See [Implicit error port on action nodes](file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes).
70	
71	> **For action nodes the instance `outputs` block is documentation, not the runtime contract.** What actually exposes the node's outputs as process-level `$vars.{nodeId}.output` is the matching `variables.nodes[]` entry — see [file-format.md — Node outputs](file-format.md#node-outputs). The BPMN emitter ignores the action-node instance `outputs` block at serialization (the manifest's `outputDefinition` drives the activity-side mapping). End / terminate nodes are the exception: their instance `outputs` block IS consumed to map workflow-level `out` variables. `uip maestro flow format` regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from the current node graph (MST-9972), so running format after structural edits self-heals an omitted entry.
72	
73	## Standard ports
74	
75	| Direction | Common name(s) | Notes |
76	| --- | --- | --- |
77	| Input (target) | `input` | Every action node accepts a single input edge on `input`. |
78	| Output (success, source) | `output`, `default`, or `success` | Name varies by plugin — `registry get` is authoritative. |
79	| Output (error, source) | `error` | Implicit on every action node via `outputs.error`. |
80	
81	Some plugins add dynamic source ports (e.g., HTTP `branch-{id}` from `inputs.branches`); those are documented in the plugin's own `impl.md`.

1	# Reference Resolution
2	
3	How to resolve reference fields — fields whose values must be looked up from another resource before create/update operations.
4	
5	> Full command syntax and options: [uip-commands.md — Integration Service](../uip-commands.md#integration-service-is). Domain-specific usage patterns are shown inline below.
6	
7	## Contents
8	- Reference IDs Are Connection-Scoped (CRITICAL)
9	- Reference Fields (CRITICAL)
10	- Scope Filtering (CRITICAL)
11	- Search References (filterPattern)
12	- Field Dependency Chains
13	- Inferring References Without Describe
14	- Static Reference-Value Labeling
15	- Validate Required Fields Before Executing
16	
17	---
18	
19	## Reference IDs Are Connection-Scoped (CRITICAL)
20	
21	Every reference ID resolves only within the account authenticated by the connection used to resolve it. A `MailFolder` ID from one Outlook mailbox is invalid in another. A Slack channel ID from one workspace is invalid in another. A Jira project ID from one Atlassian site is invalid in another.
22	
23	**Never carry a reference ID from one flow, one connection, or one session into another.** Always re-run `uip is resources run list` against the `--connection-id` bound to the current flow — even if you believe you already know the ID from a prior task or earlier in the same session.
24	
25	A reused reference ID:
26	- Passes `uip is resources describe` / `node configure` / `flow validate` cleanly (no API call checks the value against the connection).
27	- Faults at runtime when the connector tries to use the ID against a mailbox/workspace/site that does not contain it.
28	- Surfaces as a silent fault or generic "no matching resource" error — hard to diagnose without tracing back to the authoring step.
29	
30	**Rule:** resolve every reference ID fresh, against the current connection, every time. Treat any ID from your context or memory as unverified until re-listed.
31	
32	---
33	
34	## Reference Fields (CRITICAL)
35	
36	Some fields in the describe `requestFields` have a `reference` section — their value must be looked up from another resource before executing.
37	
38	### Reference structure
39	
40	```json
41	{
42	  "name": "channel",
43	  "type": "string",
44	  "displayName": "Channel name/ID",
45	  "required": true,
46	  "reference": {
47	    "objectName": "curated_channels?types=public_channel,private_channel",
48	    "lookupNames": ["name", "id"],
49	    "lookupValue": "id",
50	    "path": "/curated_channels?fields=id,name"
51	  }
52	}
53	```
54	
55	| Property | Meaning |
56	|---|---|
57	| **`reference.objectName`** | The resource to list (use as `<object>` in `run list`). May include query params. |
58	| **`reference.lookupNames`** | Fields to match the user's input against (e.g., match "general" against `name`) |
59	| **`reference.lookupValue`** | The field to extract as the resolved value (e.g., `id`) |
60	| **`reference.path`** | The API path — use `reference.objectName` for the list call |
61	| **`reference.filterPattern`** | Search endpoint pattern — substitute the user's input into `{filter}` and pass as `--query`. See [Search References](#search-references-filterpattern). |
62	| **`reference.childPath`** | Scoped child path — used for drill-down references (e.g., folder subfolders) |
63	
64	### Resolution workflow
65	
66	```bash
67	# 1. Describe → find fields with "reference" in requestFields
68	uip is resources describe "<connector-key>" "<resource>" \
69	  --connection-id "<id>" --operation Create --output json
70	
71	# 2. For each reference field, list the referenced object
72	#    Use reference.objectName as the object name (including any query params)
73	uip is resources run list "<connector-key>" "<reference.objectName>" \
74	  --connection-id "<id>" --output json
75	
76	# 3. Match the user's input against reference.lookupNames in the results
77	#    Extract reference.lookupValue as the resolved ID
78	
79	# 4. Execute with resolved IDs (not display names)
80	uip is resources run create "<connector-key>" "<resource>" \
81	  --connection-id "<id>" --body '{"channel": "<resolved-id>"}' --output json
82	```
83	
84	### Example: Resolving a Slack channel (list reference)
85	
86	User says: "Send a message to #general"
87	
88	1. **Describe** returns `channel` field with `reference.objectName: "curated_channels?types=public_channel,private_channel"`
89	2. **List** the referenced object:
90	   ```bash
91	   uip is resources run list "uipath-salesforce-slack" \
92	     "curated_channels?types=public_channel,private_channel" \
93	     --connection-id "<id>" --output json
94	   ```
95	3. **Match** "general" against `lookupNames` (`name` field) in results → find `{ "name": "general", "id": "C02CAP3LAAG" }`
96	4. **Use** the `lookupValue` (`id`) → `"C02CAP3LAAG"` in the `--body`
97	
98	**Present options to the user** when multiple matches exist. Always use the resolved `lookupValue` (not display names) in `--body` or `--query`.
99	
100	---
101	
102	## Scope Filtering (CRITICAL)
103	
104	`uip is resources run list <connector> <reference-object>` may return BOTH global entries (`scope: null`) and project-scoped entries (`scope.type: "PROJECT"`) — often with the **same display name**. Picking the first match by `.name` silently picks the wrong scope.
105	
106	**Concrete failure:** Jira issuetype "Task" exists globally as `id=3` and per-project as `id=10659` scoped to project `10851`. Selecting `id=10659` for a different project fails at runtime.
107	
108	### Rule
109	
110	When picking a reference value for a curated cascade root field (e.g. `fields.issuetype.id` on Jira), ALWAYS inspect `.scope`:
111	
112	- `scope: null` → globally applicable, safe.
113	- `scope.type: "PROJECT"` → valid only when the cascade parent (e.g. `fields.project.key`/`id`) matches `scope.project.id`.
114	
115	### jq filter
116	
117	```bash
118	uip is resources run list "<connector>" "<reference-object>" \
119	  --connection-id "<id>" --output json \
120	| jq '.Data | map(select(.scope == null or .scope.project.id == "<target-project-id>"))'
121	```
122	
123	Apply the same filter to any reference whose entries carry `scope` — not just Jira.
124	
125	---
126	
127	## Search References (filterPattern)
128	
129	Some reference fields point to **search endpoints** that require user input as a query parameter. These have a `filterPattern` property with a `{filter}` placeholder.
130	
131	### Search reference structure
132	
133	```json
134	{
135	  "name": "productId",
136	  "displayName": "Product ID",
137	  "description": "ID of the product to which the ticket is mapped",
138	  "required": false,
139	  "reference": {
140	    "objectName": "search_products",
141	    "lookupNames": ["productCode", "id"],
142	    "lookupValue": "id",
143	    "path": "/search_products",
144	    "filterPattern": "productCode={filter}"
145	  }
146	}
147	```
148	
149	### How to detect
150	
151	If `reference.filterPattern` exists, the reference supports server-side filtering. Omitting the filter does NOT reliably error — some connectors (Microsoft Graph-backed: Teams, Outlook) return the **entire unfiltered collection** instead (thousands of rows, 50/page). Arbitrary query params (`searchTerm=`, `where=`, `filter=`) are silently ignored — only the exact `filterPattern` key filters. Always apply it; never brute-force paginate a large directory when a `filterPattern` exists.
152	
153	`filterPattern` is surfaced only by `uip is resources describe` (IS-level metadata). Representations that strip it (e.g. Maestro flow `registry get` reference object, which keeps only `objectName`/`lookupValue`/`lookupNames`/`path`/`childPath`) are not authoritative — re-describe at IS level before concluding a reference cannot be filtered.
154	
155	### Resolution workflow (search)
156	
157	1. **Get the user's search input** — the value they want to look up (e.g., product name, code)
158	2. **Substitute into filterPattern** — replace `{filter}` with the user's input
159	3. **Pass as `--query`** when listing the referenced object:
160	
161	```bash
162	# filterPattern: "productCode={filter}"
163	# User input: "Widget Pro"
164	uip is resources run list "<connector-key>" "search_products" \
165	  --connection-id "<id>" --query "productCode=Widget Pro" --output json
166	```
167	
168	4. **Match results** against `lookupNames` and extract `lookupValue` as usual
169	
170	### Example: Resolving a Zoho Desk product
171	
172	User says: "Create a ticket for product Widget Pro"
173	
174	1. **Describe** returns `productId` with `reference.filterPattern: "productCode={filter}"`
175	2. **Search** with user input:
176	   ```bash
177	   uip is resources run list "uipath-zoho-desk" "search_products" \
178	     --connection-id "<id>" --query "productCode=Widget Pro" --output json
179	   ```
180	   → `{ "productCode": "WP-100", "id": "1892000000056007" }`
181	3. **Use** the `lookupValue` (`id`) → `"1892000000056007"` in `--body`
182	
183	### Example: Resolving a Microsoft Teams user (OData `$filter`)
184	
185	`filterPattern` may be a full OData `$filter` expression, not just `key={filter}`. Same mechanic: substitute `{filter}`, pass the whole string as `--query`.
186	
187	1. **Describe** the activity's object (e.g. `bot_direct_messages`) → `userId` reference has `filterPattern: "$filter=startswith(userPrincipalName,'{filter}')"`
188	2. **Substitute and pass as `--query`.** Single-quote the value so the shell does not expand the literal `$`:
189	   ```bash
190	   uip is resources run list "uipath-microsoft-teams" "users" \
191	     --connection-id "<id>" \
192	     --query '$filter=startswith(userPrincipalName,'"'"'jane.doe'"'"')' --output json
193	   ```
194	   → one row: `{ "id": "7a621d6b-…", "userPrincipalName": "jane.doe@example.com" }`
195	3. **Use** `lookupValue` (`id`) as the resolved value.
196	
197	Without the `$filter` this `/users` listing returns the full tenant directory (50/page, thousands of rows). A dedicated by-key endpoint (e.g. Teams `user-by-email/{email}`) is a fallback only when no `filterPattern` exists.
198	
199	> **If the user doesn't provide a search term**, ask them. Search references cannot be resolved without user input — do NOT call the search endpoint with an empty filter.
200	
201	---
202	
203	## Field Dependency Chains
204	
205	Some reference fields **depend on other fields** — the child field's valid values are scoped by the parent field's selection. Dependencies are expressed in `reference.path` templates containing `{otherField}` variables that must be substituted.
206	
207	### How to detect dependencies
208	
209	Check if `reference.path` contains `{fieldName}` template variables. If so, that field depends on the referenced field. Resolve the parent first.
210	
211	**CRITICAL: If a parent field value is NOT in the user's prompt, you MUST ask the user for it BEFORE attempting to resolve any child fields.** Do not resolve child fields without a scoped parent — the results will be wrong or ambiguous.
212	
213	### Dependency chain example
214	
215	A resource has two reference fields with a dependency chain:
216	
217	```
218	Field A → no template variables in path    → resolve first (list resource, pick value)
219	Field B → path contains {Field A}          → resolve after A (list scoped by A's value)
220	```
221	
222	**Wrong** — listing Field B's resource globally returns duplicates from all scopes.
223	
224	**Correct** — resolve Field A first, then list Field B's resource scoped to Field A's resolved value:
225	
226	```bash
227	# Step 1: Resolve Field A (no dependencies)
228	uip is resources run list "<connector-key>" "<resource-a>" \
229	  --connection-id "<id>" --output json
230	# → pick value
231	
232	# Step 2: Resolve Field B scoped to Field A's value
233	uip is resources run list "<connector-key>" "<resource-a>/<resolved-value>/sub-resource" \
234	  --connection-id "<id>" --output json
235	# → only values valid for this scope
236	```
237	
238	### General rule
239	
240	When resolving reference fields:
241	1. **Sort fields by dependency** — fields with no `{template}` in their reference path come first
242	2. **Resolve parent fields** — list the parent resource, pick the value
243	3. **Substitute into child path** — replace `{parentField}` in the child's reference path with the resolved value
244	4. **Resolve child fields** — list the scoped resource using the substituted path
245	
246	This pattern applies across all connectors wherever child fields are scoped by parent selections.
247	
248	---
249	
250	## Inferring References Without Describe
251	
252	When describe metadata is unavailable (see [resources.md — Describe Failures](resources.md#describe-failures)), infer reference fields from naming conventions:
253	
254	- Fields ending in **`Id`** (e.g., `PromotionId`, `AccountId`) typically reference the object with the matching base name (`Promotion`, `Account`).
255	- List the inferred object to resolve the ID: `is resources run list "<connector-key>" "<base-name>" --connection-id "<id>" --output json`
256	- Match the user's value by `Name` or `DisplayName` in the results.
257	
258	---
259	
260	## Static Reference-Value Labeling
261	
262	When baking a **static value** for a field that has a `.reference` block (any connector — Jira `fields.project.key`/`fields.issuetype.id`, Slack `send_as`/`channel`, Outlook `outputTimezone`/`calendarID`, etc.), the AgentHub edit-UI cannot resolve the display label on its own and renders the raw scalar. Persist labels alongside the bound values via `designTimeMetadata.designTimeLookups`.
263	
264	### Persisted shape
265	
266	```jsonc
267	"designTimeMetadata": {
268	  "designTimeLookups": {
269	    "<dotted-field-name>": "<displayName> - <value>"
270	    // e.g. "fields.project.key": "Orchestrator - OR"
271	    // e.g. "fields.issuetype.id": "Task - 3"
272	    // e.g. "send_as": "Bot - bot"
273	    // e.g. "channel": "general - C02CAP3LAAG"
274	  }
275	}
276	```
277	
278	- Shape is `Record<string, string>`. NOT the array-of-`{id,title}` form that the FE library's TypeScript types may suggest — that is the internal Redux shape, different from persistence.
279	- Key = the same dotted field name used in `staticValues.<bucket>.<field>`.
280	- Value = `"<displayName> - <baked-value>"` (literal ` - ` separator).
281	
282	### Resolving `displayName`
283	
284	```bash
285	uip is resources run list "<connector>" "<reference.objectName>" \
286	  --connection-id "<id>" --output json
287	```
288	
289	Match the baked value against `lookupValue` (from the field's `reference` block). Take `lookupNames[0]` from the matching entry as `displayName`.
290	
291	### Cascade-scoped references
292	
293	When `reference.path` contains `{parent.field}` placeholders (e.g. Jira `fields.issuetype.id` → `/project/{fields.project.key}/issuetypes`), the reference is logically scoped to a parent value but the CLI's `run list` does not accept a parent-context flag. `reference.objectName` in this case names the path's root (`project`), not the leaf collection you actually want.
294	
295	Two-step resolution:
296	
297	1. **Pick the leaf object.** Take the last path segment singular form. For `/project/{fields.project.key}/issuetypes` use `issuetype` (drop trailing `s` if present).
298	2. **List the leaf object and filter by scope.** Many connectors return both global (`scope: null`) and parent-scoped rows in the same listing:
299	   ```bash
300	   uip is resources run list "<connector>" "<leaf-object>" \
301	     --connection-id "<id>" --output json
302	   ```
303	   - If your baked value resolves to a global entry, pick the row with `scope: null`.
304	   - If it resolves to a parent-scoped entry, pick the row whose `scope.<parentType>.<id>` matches the baked parent value (resolved through its own reference first).
305	   - Match by `reference.lookupValue` as in the flat case. Take `reference.lookupNames[0]` as the label.
306	
307	Concrete Jira example — baked `fields.project.key="OR"`, `fields.issuetype.id="3"`:
308	- Project: `run list … project` → match `key=OR` → `name="Orchestrator"` → `"Orchestrator - OR"`.
309	- Issuetype: `run list … issuetype` returns ~400+ rows. `id=3` matches `name="Task"` → `"Task - 3"`.
310	
311	**Jira issuetype scope caveat.** The CLI surfaces every issuetype row with `scope: null` even when Jira itself project-scopes the type (the connector flattens scope). Filtering by `scope` is therefore unreliable for Jira issuetype disambiguation. When multiple rows share a display name (e.g., several `Epic` entries at different ids), verify the candidate id by re-running the cascade describe with `(project.key, issuetype.id)` — a successful describe means the id is valid for that project. Other connectors that return scope honestly still match by `scope.<parentType>.<id>` as described above.
312	
313	Do NOT re-issue `uip is resources describe -f <parent>=<value>` solely for label resolution — the cascade is intended for required-field expansion. For Jira `curated_create_issue` specifically, omit `--action`; passing it triggers `No api-type ObjectAction matched for fields [...]`.
314	
315	### Applies to
316	
317	Every connector with reference-typed fields. Emit one `designTimeLookups` entry per static reference value baked into `staticValues` — Jira, Slack, Outlook, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Workday, and so on.
318	
319	---
320	
321	## Validate Required Fields Before Executing
322	
323	After resolving references, **check every required field** from the describe response against what the user provided. This is a hard gate — do NOT execute until all required fields have values.
324	
325	**Process:**
326	1. Collect all fields where `required: true` from the describe output
327	2. For each required field, check if the user's prompt contains a value for it
328	3. If any required field is missing, **ask the user** before proceeding:
329	   - List the missing fields with their `displayName` and `description`
330	   - For reference fields, explain what kind of value is expected
331	   - Wait for the user's response before continuing
332	4. Only after all required fields are accounted for, proceed to execute
333	
334	> **Do NOT guess or skip missing required fields.** A missing required field will cause a runtime error. It is always better to ask than to assume.
